data.narrative:
LuxWall, a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Scott Thomsen, has raised $84M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private firms and 1 public company (ticker: LNZA) operating in the same sector, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $84M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $160M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median valuation across these three peers is $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $136M (low), $580M (median), and $1.1B (high). The dispersion reflects material uncertainty around LuxWall's positioning within the peer set. Stage-progression conservatively anchors the low end, while peer medians reflect later-stage capital efficiency and market maturation. Key uncertainties include LuxWall's operational progress relative to Series C peers, capital efficiency trajectory, and technology differentiation within an active funding environment.
